searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent. Several searches blocked the author's own domains so the second source would be independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or hedged.

1791, Wolvaart, Nederburgh, the manor house of 1800 and national monument: Bibendum, South African Wines, Portfolio. Granted changed to acquired.
Cape Fine and Rare Wine Auction of 2019 at the Rupert Museum, Stellenbosch: drinks international, Herald, Winemag. Sound.
Wine of Origin: IWSC guide gives Western Cape for 2012; Jancis Robinson files 2011 as Stellenbosch. Hedged to the vintage.

swaps.ruling: No swap proposed by the author. Perdeberg's Courageous stands under the thin region rule; Rex Equus, the cellar's limited red, is a possible alternative flagship but no source read names it the head of the range, so no swap is opened. Plaisir de Merle not needed.

codexTension: The region record's Paarl summary dates Nederburg to 1791 and calls Edelkeur its botrytised Chenin: in agreement. No tension found.
planWhys: Perdeberg's plan note names a Rex Equus range of 2021: Rex Equus existed by 2014 and the 2021 release was its Pioneer's Blend 2019 for the eightieth year.
KWV's why: governed the trade for seventy years stands loosely; the act of 1924 gave control of distilling wine and surplus, and the powers waned from the early 1990s.
